/kind bug

> podSandboxes are needed, we cannot just silence the error like this

When kubelet is running, if a podSandbox is lost, kubelet will recreate the pod and containerGC while delete old orphan containers.
so I think that if a podSandbox is lost during the kubelet restarting, kubelet should not panic, it should be able to start normally, after the kubelet is started, the sandbox and containers should be recreate and old orphan containers should be gc.

I need an external pov though...

@chenyw1990 I am curious, how k8s handler containers without the sandbox container? Will it restart the pod?
In general, reconcile loop under the CPU manager should remove the stale state, so it should not be a problem to log a warning instead of dropping the error.
/test pull-kubernetes-node-kubelet-serial-cpu-manager

@cynepco3hahue 
There are two scenarios,
1. The pod is no longer running on the current node. Kubelet.HandlePodCleanups() will clear the container.
2. If the pod is still running on the node, kubelet.SyncPod() detects that the sandbox of the pod is lost, deletes  the orphaned container, and rebuilds the sandbox and container.

> @cynepco3hahue
> There are two scenarios,
> 
> 1. The pod is no longer running on the current node. Kubelet.HandlePodCleanups() will clear the container.
> 2. If the pod is still running on the node, kubelet.SyncPod() detects that the sandbox of the pod is lost, deletes  the orphaned container, and rebuilds the sandbox and container.

Thanks for the clarification, in this case, I think it good to go.
/lgtm

issue_context.title: kubelet will panic when pause container lose during kubelet restarting
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
with --cpu-manager-policy=static
kubelet will panic when pause container lose during kubelet restarting

**What you expected to happen**:
kubelet can start normally

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1,config kubelet with --cpu-manager-policy=static
2, Run a large number of pods on the test node
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
  labels:
    app: test
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test
  replicas: 25
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 50%
      maxUnavailable: 0
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: test1
        image: nginx:1.14.2
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["sleep", "1000000"]
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 5m
            memory: 10Mi
        ports:
        - containerPort: 81
          name: test
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: test-conf-file
          subPathExpr: test
      - name: test2
        image: nginx:1.14.2
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["sleep", "1000000"]
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 5m
            memory: 10Mi
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - cat
            - /dev/null
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        ports:
        - containerPort: 82
          name: test
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: test-conf-file
          subPathExpr: test
      volumes:
      - name: test-conf-file
        hostPath:
          path: /data
          type: Directory
```


3,stop kubelet use command: `systemctl  stop kubelet`
4,kill and remove all the pause container like this:
```
for line in `docker ps | grep test | grep "pause" | awk '{print $1}'` ; do  echo $line; docker kill $line; docker rm $line; done
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1468240/105174877-24f4ab80-5b5e-11eb-8872-ef930ced8e06.png)

5,start kubelet use command: `systemctl start kubelet`
